summary: Long quiet period during streaming response leads to socket termination and partial payload for enterprise customer
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running streaming chat responses (SSE and WebSocket) sometimes close the connection after a prolonged quiet period while the model is still generating. Impact: Partial messages delivered to end users causing application-level errors and loss of context for follow-up prompts. Observed repeatedly during peak traffic windows and correlates with backend tail-latency spikes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer agent that subscribes to SSE or WebSocket streaming endpoint with keepalive disabled by default. 2) Send a long-generation prompt (>= 1200 tokens expected) which triggers multi-second decoder stalls (typical for redwood-3b-chat-v1 under long context). 3) Observe an extended interval (>6s) of no data sent from backend, then client sees 'connection reset' or the stream ends with HTTP 200 but truncated payload. 4) Reproduce under prod-us-east during simulated burst load or python client that disables client heartbeats.
logs:
[2026-03-10T15:09:11Z] proxy: conn_id=98765 keepalive=0 idle_period=7.4s -> drop connection; upstream_status=200 partial_bytes=1423
[2026-03-10T15:09:08Z] runtime: request=0x7f4b token_delay=6.8s kv-cache-hit=false batch_size=1 gpu_util=62%
[2026-03-10T15:09:09Z] gw: 502 returned during fallback to model-quantized; fallback_success=false
Customer-provided client logs: "stream closed unexpectedly after 00:00:12 while waiting for next SSE event"
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Customer submitted with screenshots and a sample client trace. They say this occurs ~3-4 times per hour during high-load windows. Attachments: client-trace-20260310.txt, pcap-sample.zip.

2026-03-10 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. Asking for request_id and exact timestamps; requested reproducer and whether customer uses keep-alive or proxied client. Assigned to runtime on-call.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Anika Rao): Verified proxy logs show idle client connections closed by streaming-proxy after idle_timeout (7s) when backend is silent. Notable: proxy interprets multi-second generator stalls as idle rather than active generation. Investigating keepalive semantics between runtime and proxy.
2026-03-11 - Customer (SageLex): We do not send application-level heartbeats. Our Electron client relies on the SSE stream continuously. Can the platform avoid closing when model is still working?

2026-03-12 - Runtime Eng (Diego Marquez): Reproduced locally with long-context prompt and found decoder stalls triggered by kv-cache eviction and model compilation fallback under memory pressure. Adding an experimental heartbeat from runtime to proxy prevents proxy from closing. Preparing draft PR to extend proxy idle timeout and emit intermittent SSE comment tokens (":heartbeat:") as a mitigation.

2026-03-12 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Notified customer of workaround: enable client keepalive or we can enable server-side heartbeat for their org while fix is prepared. Customer prefers server-side change.
2026-03-12 - Customer: Requested ETA on server-side mitigation and asked for note about billing impact for additional SSE bytes.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: proxy idle_timeout too low for occasional multi-second decode stalls; proxy treats silence as dead connection and forcibly closes TCP.
Correlated spikes with GPU memory pressure events and kernel fallback in serving-runtime which cause bursts of extra decode time (5-9s).
Observed that when runtime falls back from tensor-core kernel to fallback path, no intermediate SSE flush is emitted until chunk completes, creating long quiet periods that exceed proxy idle_timeout.
Heap/profile traces: model attention kv-cache thrashing on long context (>= 8k tokens) leading to periodic GC-like stalls in C++ runtime.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied 2026-03-12: Enabled server-side intermittent comment heartbeats for SageLex org (emit '\u003c!--heartbeat--\u003e' SSE events every 3s during streaming when no model tokens emitted). Verified client stays connected and receives full payloads during long decodes.
Short-term fix: increased streaming-proxy idle_timeout from 7s to 12s for affected prod-us-east fleet while a runtime PR is tested.

Planned long-term fixes: (1) runtime PR #924 to emit periodic progress pings when decode path stalls (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/924). (2) optimize kv-cache eviction to reduce decode stalls and add metrics to detect fallback kernel usage. (3) update platform default proxy timeout to 10s for streaming endpoints and publish guidance in Streaming Timeout Runbook.
Billing note: Heartbeat events are small (<= 12 bytes) but count toward request bytes; CS has prepared a billing override for affected customers if needed. Notified Finance.
Follow-ups: Create INT ticket to schedule runtime change rollout and monitoring alert: 'streaming-generator-silence > 5s without end-of-stream' (linked INT-41833).
